title: Content salvage and material suitability
audience: Coordinators, supervisors and trained workers who may be asked about, triage, refer or document cleaning and salvage after a fire or smoke event. Not a qualification or authority to enter a fire-damaged building, release it, or certify it as safe.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish salvageable items from items that need specialist or client decisions, and refuse the immediate handling of damaged electronics.

instruction.heading: Scope and authority
instruction.body: This lesson teaches how to list, prioritise and record fire- and smoke-affected contents, and when to refer them. It does not allow cleaning, testing or operating electronics, appliances or heritage items. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.

instruction.heading: Content salvage and material suitability
instruction.body: Catalogue the items, establish who owns them, set salvage priorities, and seek qualified guidance for heat-damaged electronics, fragile finishes and heritage objects. Secure the client's consent and record any repairability that is uncertain. A homeowner who asks that smoke-affected photographs and electronics be wiped immediately is asking for work that has not been assessed. Do not operate exposed electrical devices without authorisation. Keep a salvage register that distinguishes protected items, items needing restricted handling and items that need professional referral. In training, complete a mock salvage register using fictional items.

procedure: Do not operate any exposed electrical device until the responsible person authorises it.
Catalogue each item with its location, condition and dated photographs.
Confirm ownership of each item and record the owner's consent to each decision.
Set salvage priorities. Separate protected items, items needing restricted handling and items needing professional referral.
Refer heat-damaged electronics, fragile finishes and heritage objects for qualified guidance.
Keep the salvage decision log and record any repairability that is uncertain.

workedExamples.situation: A homeowner asks that smoke-affected photographs and electronics be wiped immediately.
workedExamples.reasoning: Hold the items, record the request and refer them for assessment and owner consent. Do not operate exposed electrical devices. Wiping is work that has not been assessed.

workedExamples.situation: A technician plugs in a smoke-damaged laptop to see whether it still works.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Operating an exposed electrical device without authorisation is refused. Record the item and refer it.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves and bags for handling items, selected from the hazard assessment.
Labelled bags and tags for each item, with the register number.

commonErrors.error: Wiping or operating smoke-affected electronics to see whether they work.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not operate exposed electrical devices without authorisation. Record and refer.

commonErrors.error: Disposing of contents because they smell of smoke.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the item and the owner's decision. Disposal needs consent and an assessment.

commonErrors.error: Keeping no register of what was moved.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a salvage register that records each item's location, photographs and decision.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not authorise handling or disposal of contents beyond recording and referral. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.
Heat-damaged electronics and heritage objects need qualified guidance before any cleaning or operation.

qualityStandard: The learner records each item with photographs and an owner decision.
The learner separates protected items from items that need referral.
The learner refuses to operate exposed electrical devices.
documentationEvidence: Salvage decision log: item, location, condition, photographs, owner consent, referral.
Compatibility review note for any finish or heritage item.
summary: Electronics are not operated without authorisation.
Consent and referral come before any cleaning or disposal.

knowledgeChecks.question: A homeowner asks for smoke-affected photographs and electronics to be wiped immediately. What is correct?
options: Wipe them now, because the owner asked and the owner is the one who pays for the whole clean-up of the house
Hold them, record the request and refer the items for assessment and owner consent. Do not operate exposed electrical devices.
Plug in the electronics to test them, then wipe them down once they are confirmed to be working properly for the owner

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the correct first action for a damaged item of unknown condition?
options: Clean and test it at once
Record it in the salvage register with photographs and refer it for assessment
Dispose of it because it is smoke-damaged

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: Fire-scene release, structural and utility isolation, asbestos assessment and removal, and some waste handling are restricted to competent and, where the law requires, licensed people, and may be controlled by fire investigators, the police, structural engineers, utilities or the building owner. Insurer and owner permission do not replace a release from the authority that controls the site. Where that authority is not identified, do not proceed.

stopWorkAndReferral: Stop and refer when exposed electrical devices would be operated without authority.
A stop-work decision is correct, so record it and restart only once the competent party confirms the scope in writing.
